newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Sonasid '97 net income seen up.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Sonasid '97 net income seen up.

text.p: Morocco's partly privatised steel mill giant Sonasid is expected to post net income of 180 million dirhams ($20.4 million) in 1997, up 20 percent over the 1996 period, a stockbroker said on Monday.
Stockbroker Casablanca Finance Intermediation (CFI) said the firm's net income is estimated at 150 million dirhams in 1996. CFI led Sonasid's privatisation operation.
The plant also forecasts a rise in value of steel sales to 1.8 billion dirhams in 1997 from an estimated 1.7 billion dirhams in 1996.
Sonasid sold an estimated 439,000 tonnes of steel products, mainly reinforcing bars and wire rods. It plans to reach 450,000 tonnes by end 1997, CFI said.
"The expected improvement of the firm's income is due largely to decreasing tariffs on steel products and lower interest charges next year," a CFI market analyst said.
The end of a cycle of long term debt repayment will have a positive impact on the firm's business, he said.
The government sold 35 percent of Sonasid stock through the Casablanca bourse earlier this year. The flotation was worth $48 million.
The ministry of privatisation is campaigning for the sale of up to 51 percent of Sonasid to set up a hard core of investors including foreigners but with no results yet, an official said.
One of the 46 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, Sonasid was last traded at 329 dirhams per share.
The Moroccan government plans to have completed the sale of 114 state enterprises and hotels by 1998. It has already sold its stakes in 46 firms worth 9.7 billion dirhams since November 1993.
